territorial_scope.description: Applies to health care service plans and disability insurers subject to California's Health and Safety Code and Insurance Code.

evidence.quote: A health care service plan, including a specialized health care service plan that uses an artificial intelligence, algorithm, or other software tool

agora_applications: Medicine, life sciences and public health

summary.short: Amends California Health and Safety Code §1367.01 and Insurance Code §10123.135 to regulate health plans and disability insurers using AI or algorithms in utilization review. Such tools may not deny, delay or modify care based on medical necessity; a licensed physician or health care professional must decide.
summary.long: Section 1 amends Health and Safety Code §1367.01 for health care service plans, including specialized plans, and entities that use AI, algorithm or software tools for utilization review based on medical necessity. The plan must ensure the tool bases determinations on the enrollee's clinical history and individual circumstances, does not rely solely on a group dataset, does not supplant provider decisionmaking, does not discriminate, is fairly applied, is open to department inspection, and does not directly or indirectly harm enrollees. The tool may not deny, delay or modify services; only a licensed physician or qualified health professional may make that determination. Plans must document AI use in written policies, periodically review performance, and limit patient data use. The department may issue guidance within one year of federal rules. Section 2 adds parallel requirements for disability insurers in Insurance Code §10123.135, including annual review of criteria. The director or commissioner may assess administrative penalties by order for each failure to meet timeframes or other requirements; amounts are not stated. Section 3 states that no state reimbursement is required for local agencies. No effective date is stated in the text.},

notes: The document is the bill text (SECs 1-3) without underline or strikeout marking, so unchanged restated text cannot be separated from new text; both amended sections are shown in full. No effective date appears in the text. The 'department' in both amended sections is not named in this excerpt. Internal differences between parallel provisions: § 1367.01(k)(1)(G) refers to inspection 'pursuant to Section 1381', but § 10123.135(j)(1)(G) does not; § 1367.01(k)(5) lets 'the department and the State Department of Health Care Services' issue guidance, while § 10123.135(j)(5) names only 'the department'. § 10123.135(h)(5) refers to 'enrollee' although that section concerns insureds. SEC. 3 is a state-mandate statement with no operative obligation.
